data.name: Ajhar
data.gender_notes: Ajhar is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: This name is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Ajah' which means 'not born'. The name Ajhar is formed by prefixing the syllable 'Aj' to the root 'Har'. 'Aj' is derived from 'Ajit', a name of Lord Vishnu. 'Har' is derived from 'Hari', a name of Lord Vishnu, symbolizing victory. Thus, Ajhar signifies the victory of Lord Vishnu or Lord Ajit.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the victory of the divine over the material world.
data.etymology: Ajhar belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord Ajit's victory.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ajhar total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: The name Ajhar is a rare yet beautiful name in the Indian subcontinent. In Indian cultural context, the name signifies a powerful and victorious person. Ajhar is believed to be a name of a warrior and a leader. The name carries a sense of strength and courage.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, Ajhar is a name of Lord Vishnu who is believed to have never been born (Ajah), but yet he exists in all forms. He is also known as Lord Ajit, the Indestructible and Invincible. Thus, the name Ajhar embodies the power, victory, and invincibility of Lord Vishnu, and inspires a sense of divine connection and spiritual strength in the bearer of the name.
